topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the context for the cancer lecture series, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Biological foundations and origin factors of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explain how endogenous cellular errors, environmental mutagens, and inherited traits contribute to its onset.

topics.label: Environmental exposures, chance, and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore common environmental mutagens, the scientific debate over bad luck versus exposure, and global epidemiological variations in cancer rates.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how pathogens promote cancer, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular link between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary toxins, UV radiation, and metabolically activated chemicals induce DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host context, and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and host developmental stages facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic signatures, epidemiological approaches, and experimental assays used to detect and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the lecture and discusses the practical balancing of risks and benefits associated with environmental carcinogen exposures.
